import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 160

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/160](https://www.erdosproblems.com/160)
-/

namespace Erdos160

/--
Let $h(n)$ be the smallest $k$ such that $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ can be coloured with $k$ colours
so that every four-term arithmetic progression must contain at least three distinct colours.
-/
noncomputable def erdos_160.h (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
    sInf {k | ∃ (colouring : Finset.Icc 1 n → Fin k), ∀ (progression : Set ℕ),
    (progression ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n ∧ progression.IsAPOfLength 4) →
    3 ≤ (colouring '' {k | (k : ℕ) ∈ progression}).ncard}


open Filter

/--
On [Mathoverflow](https://mathoverflow.net/a/410815) user
[leechlattice](https://mathoverflow.net/users/125498/leechlattice) shows that
$h(n) \ll n^{\frac 2 3}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.known_upper :
    (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) := by
  sorry

open Real

/--
Estimate $h(n)$ by finding a better upper bound.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.better_upper :
    let upper_bound : ℕ → ℝ := answer(sorry)
    (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] upper_bound ∧
    upper_bound =o[atTop] fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) := by
  sorry

/--
Estimate $h(n)$ by finding a better lower bound.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.better_lower:
    let lower_bound : ℕ → ℝ := answer(sorry)
    (lower_bound =O[atTop] fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ c > 0,
    (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =O[atTop] (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) →
    ∀ c > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =o[atTop] lower_bound := by
  sorry

/--
The observation of Zachary Hunter in [that question](https://mathoverflow.net/q/410808)
coupled with the bounds of Kelley-Meka [KeMe23](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.05537) imply that
$$h(N) \gg \exp(c(\log N)^{\frac 1 {12}})$$
for some $c > 0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.variants.known_lower :
    ∃ c > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12)))
    =O[atTop] fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ):= by
  sorry

end Erdos160

status_issues.source_status: The source records Hunter’s improvement h(N) ≪ N^(log(3)/log(22) + o(1)), with log(3)/log(22) approximately 0.355. Hunter posted this on 18 October 2025, and the result is incorporated into the main problem page. This already satisfies this declaration’s particular improvement target, although the overall estimation problem remains open.

status_issues.source_status: The source records h(N) ≫ exp(c₀ (log N)^(1/9)) for some c₀ > 0, from Hunter’s observation combined with Bloom–Sisask’s 2023 improvement. This satisfies even the declaration’s requirement to dominate exp(c (log n)^(1/12)) for every positive c.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/160 states the 1/9 bound. Bloom–Sisask, arXiv:2309.02353, Theorem 1, proves the corresponding bound for three-term-AP-free subsets.
status_issues.suggested_change: Mark this particular theorem `research solved`. An explicit answer not requiring identification of c₀ is `fun n : ℕ => Real.exp (Real.log (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10))`: it is O(h(n)) by the 1/9 bound, while exp(c (log n)^(1/12)) is little-o of it for every c > 0. This implication from the source’s bound was verified in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The file follows the webpage and MathOverflow in using the first number of colours admitting an avoiding colouring. Erdős’s original 1989 paper instead uses the last number of classes for which every partition forces a four-term AP in the union of two classes.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For N ≥ 4, write H(N) for the file’s threshold. An avoiding colouring exists, and admissibility is upward-closed in the number of available colours. Consequently the forcing numbers are exactly those below H(N), so the original threshold is H(N) − 1. This is an exact one-colour reparameterization, not equality of the two functions. Since H(N) ≥ 3 for N ≥ 4, the thresholds bound each other by constant multiples; all asymptotic bounds and improvement requests in this file are unchanged. The threshold identity was verified in Lean using failure of admissibility as the forcing predicate; the complete partition-language translation and asymptotic equivalence were checked mathematically.

sources_consulted: Kelley–Meka, Strong Bounds for 3-Progressions, arXiv:2302.05537v6, LaTeX source, especially Theorem 1.2: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.05537
Bloom–Sisask, An improvement to the Kelley-Meka bounds on three-term arithmetic progressions, arXiv:2309.02353, LaTeX source, Theorem 1: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02353
Deng–Tidor–Zhao, Uniform sets with few progressions via colorings, arXiv:2307.06914v2, LaTeX source, explicit 22-point colouring and tensor-power lemma: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.06914

Erdős, Some Problems and Results on Combinatorial Number Theory, Ann. New York Acad. Sci. 576 (1989), 132–145, paragraph beginning ‘Freud and I tried to investigate’: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1989-35.pdf
review.notes: All five declarations were checked. The admissible-colour set is nonempty for every n, so Nat.sInf’s empty-set default is never used. Lean proofs establish h(0)=0, h(1)=h(2)=h(3)=1, and h(4)=3; finite enumeration agrees through n=7. AP distinctness, finite image cardinality, real exponents, and logarithm boundary cases were checked. The guard in better_lower is activated by known_lower and is not vacuous. Consolidated checks compile in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using sorry-backed problem theorems. The two historical solved bounds remain correctly stated. Erdős webpages and the original scan were read through a reader proxy when necessary. No repository files were edited.
